c.tagline: The Catalan capital of France — sun-baked squares and a Majorcan palace between the Pyrenees and the Mediterranean.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered; both Uber and Bolt operate. Ranks are at the railway station and near Le Castillet.

emergency.note: 112 is the Europe-wide emergency number connecting to police, ambulance and fire, free from any phone.

hood_landmark.Porte d'Espagne: Bois des Pins, Porte d'Espagne, Perpignan

avoid.reason: The run-down Saint-Jacques quarter and parts of Bas-Vernet are best avoided at night due to poverty-linked street crime.
Pickpocketing occurs around the train station and old-town lanes, especially after dark.

hood_desc: The pedestrian old-town core around Le Castillet, Place de la Loge and the Saint-Jean cathedral, climbing to the Palace of the Kings of Majorca; the best base for first-timers, with the main sights and Catalan squares on foot.
The bustling area around Perpignan's railway station — once dubbed by Dalí 'the centre of the world' — handy for TGV connections to Barcelona and Paris and packed with mid-range hotels.
A characterful, largely residential old quarter of narrow Catalan streets just south of the centre, quieter and more local while still walkable to the sights.
A leafy residential district on the southern edge of the city with parkland and easier parking; calm and green, suited to travellers with a car or wanting quiet.

Perpignan's southern gateway along Avenue d'Espagne, where the A9 motorway exit and the Mas Palegry business parks back onto the pine woods of the Bois des Pins. Spread out and car-dependent about 3 km from the old town, it holds most of the city's garden and roadside hotels, including the Villa Duflot.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 6am to 8:30pm, with limited evening services.
transit.note: The Sankéo network runs the city and suburban buses; the flat, compact centre around Le Castillet is easily walked, and free electric 'P'tit Bus' shuttles loop the old town.
transit.pay: Buy tickets from the driver or Sankéo machines and validate on board; a single ride is about €1.10 and a day pass about €3.

bus: Perpignan bus station (Gare Routière) — regional liÓ coaches and FlixBus
train: Gare de Perpignan — TGV to Paris and Barcelona, TER regional services

transit.m: Sankéo bus/navette between the airport and the city centre and station (~20 min)
Taxi from the airport to the centre (~15 min)

tip.r: Service is included (service compris); leaving a few coins or rounding up ~5% for good service is customary but optional.

landmarks: Palais des Rois de Majorque (Palace of the Kings of Majorca)
A vast 13th-century Gothic palace-fortress crowning the city, its ramparts, chapel and courtyards recalling Perpignan's brief reign as a Mediterranean royal capital.
Le Castillet
The crenellated red-brick gate-tower that is Perpignan's emblem, once a prison, now the Casa Pairal museum of Catalan folk traditions with rooftop views.
Cathédrale Saint-Jean-Baptiste
A single-nave Gothic cathedral begun in 1324, notable for its pebble-and-brick facade, wrought-iron campanile and the poignant Devout Christ crucifix.
Campo Santo
France's only surviving medieval cloister-cemetery, a serene 14th-century quadrangle of white marble arcades that hosts summer music festivals.
Place de la Loge & Loge de Mer
The polished-marble heart of old Perpignan, where the 14th-century maritime exchange, town hall and Aristide Maillol bronzes anchor café-filled Catalan evenings.
Musée d'art Hyacinthe Rigaud
An elegant hôtel particulier honoring Perpignan-born royal portraitist Rigaud, with collections running from Gothic altarpieces to Picasso, Dufy and Maillol.
Casa Xanxo
A rare surviving Gothic merchant's mansion of 1507, its sculpted frieze of the Seven Deadly Sins fronting exhibitions on the city's heritage.
Église Saint-Jacques & Jardin la Miranda
A 13th-century church of the Sanch penitent brotherhood in the old gypsy quarter, beside a hidden garden atop the medieval ramparts.
Hôtel Pams
An opulent Belle Époque mansion built on cigarette-paper fortunes, its gilded staircase, painted ceilings and Venetian courtyard open free to visitors.
Collioure
The jewel-box harbor town twenty minutes away, whose royal castle, pink bell tower and Fauvist light seduced Matisse and Derain.

train.note: Perpignan's station - the one Salvador Dali called the centre of the universe - is about 15 minutes' walk west of the old town. It is the last French stop on the Paris-Barcelona high-speed line, so the daily through TGV calls here and reaches Barcelona Sants in around 1h30m, with Renfe AVE services on the same route. There is also a cheap slow alternative: a TER liO train to Cerbere, then a Rodalies local across the border to Portbou and Figueres, which needs a change and separate tickets. Paris is about 5 hours by direct TGV. French and Spanish fares are sold separately even where the train is the same, so compare renfe.com and SNCF Connect.

bus.note: Coaches use the bus station beside the railway station on Avenue du General de Gaulle. Barcelona is about 3 hours by coach and there are also direct runs to Barcelona airport and to Andorra la Vella, useful because no train reaches Andorra. Cars liO regional coaches (https://www.lio-occitanie.fr/) cover Collioure, Ceret, Font-Romeu and the Cote Vermeille at a low flat fare paid on board, and the narrow-gauge Train Jaune into the Pyrenees connects at Villefranche-de-Conflent. Book international coaches online; carry ID for the Spanish border.

ferry.note: Perpignan is about 13 km inland and has no ferry service of its own. Nearby Port-Vendres, 30 minutes away by train, handles cargo and occasional cruise calls rather than scheduled passenger sailings, and the boats from Collioure and Argeles are summer coastal excursions. The nearest scheduled ferries are at Barcelona, about 90 minutes away by train, and at Sete, where Corsica Ferries sails to Corsica, Sardinia and the Balearics (https://www.corsica-ferries.fr/).

half.name: Céret
half.blurb: A Catalan market town known for its cherries and a modern art museum lies about thirty minutes from Perpignan.

half.name: Prades
half.blurb: This gateway to Mont Canigou sits near the Abbaye Saint-Michel-de-Cuxa, roughly forty-five minutes away.

half.name: Girona
half.blurb: A walled medieval city with a Jewish quarter and cathedral steps lies about an hour across the Spanish border.

half.name: Figueres
half.blurb: The Dalí Theatre-Museum draws visitors to this Catalan town roughly forty-five minutes into Spain.
